a: Kloof Road, The Glen, Camps Bay
q: Salsify at the Roundhouse Cape Town
s: A tasting-menu restaurant built into the curved stone walls of a 1786 guardhouse, perched above Camps Bay with the Atlantic filling every window.
w: Chef Ryan Cole's dining room occupies the surviving foundations of the Old Roundhouse, a guardhouse and hunting lodge built for the Cape garrison in 1786 and now a national monument above Camps Bay. The multi-course tasting menu leans on Cape ingredients and classical technique, backed by chef Luke Dale-Roberts.
_facts: Occupies the Old Roundhouse, an 18th-century guardhouse and national monument
Chef Ryan Cole, backed by Luke Dale-Roberts

s: A fifth-floor dining room above Parliament Street pairing Japanese technique with South African ingredients, run by the country's first Three Knives chef.
w: FYN sits on the fifth floor of Speaker's Corner on Parliament Street, where chef Peter Tempelhoff and culinary director Ashley Moss build tasting menus around washoku technique and Cape produce -- abalone, wagyu, indigenous herbs. On the World's 50 Best list every year since 2021.
_facts: Chef Peter Tempelhoff with Ashley Moss
Eat Out Restaurant of the Year, 2026

s: A single tasting menu served inside a 1796 Constantia wine estate, rebuilt weekly around what the estate's own soil produces.
w: Beyond occupies the manor house and cellars of Buitenverwachting, a wine estate dating to 1796 in the Constantia valley. Chef Peter Tempelhoff (also of FYN) designed the menu around strict seasonality, served among vineyards at the foot of the Constantiaberg.
_facts: Set on Buitenverwachting wine estate, established 1796
Chef Peter Tempelhoff, same as FYN

s: A Mediterranean dining room facing the Atlantic on Bantry Bay's seafront strip, open since October 2024 and voted Africa's best new restaurant within a year.
w: Amare opened in Bantry Bay in October 2024, cooking Mediterranean dishes drawn from the coastlines of France, Greece, Italy, Portugal and Spain, facing the Atlantic on Victoria Road. In November 2025 it was named Africa's Best New Restaurant at the World Culinary Awards.
_facts: Named Africa's Best New Restaurant 2025, World Culinary Awards

s: A dining room on the only street in the world to have housed two Nobel Peace Prize laureates, with a wine cellar below and a cigar balcony over the Orlando cooling towers.
w: 1947 on Vilakazi Street opened in 2021, founded by Naomi Lele Ratsheko and named for the birth year of both her parents. It sits steps from both the Mandela family home and Archbishop Desmond Tutu's former house. Chef Junior Kotane's menu runs from burgers and pasta to South African staples.
_facts: On Vilakazi Street -- the only street with two Nobel Peace Prize laureates' former homes

a: Royal Mansour, Rue Abou El Abbas Sebti
q: La Grande Table Marocaine Royal Mansour Marrakech
s: A formal Moroccan dining room inside the Royal Mansour, built around tagines and pastilla prepared by an all-female kitchen brigade of local dadas.
w: La Grande Table Marocaine occupies its own pavilion within the Royal Mansour, the hotel built by King Mohammed VI in Marrakech's Hivernage district. The kitchen is staffed by Moroccan dadas -- traditional female home cooks -- preparing tagines, pastilla and couscous refined for a formal room. Ranked 19th on MENA's 50 Best 2026.

s: Three Michelin stars in a glass-walled dining room overlooking the fjord, steps from the Opera House.
w: Chef Esben Holmboe Bang built Maaemo on a single premise -- organic, biodynamic, or wild, nothing else -- and it has held three Michelin stars since 2019. The tasting menu tracks the Norwegian coast and forest floor season by season, in the Barcode district by the harbour.
_facts: Three Michelin stars, Norway's only restaurant at that tier

s: Two Michelin stars and a Green Star in a converted industrial building above the Akerselva.
w: Mikael Svensson's Kontrast runs on a strict seasonal-Norwegian, low-waste ethic that earned it a Michelin Green Star alongside its two stars -- produce dictates the menu. It sits in Vulkan, the old industrial quarter turned food quarter, near Mathallen market hall.
_facts: Two Michelin stars plus Green Star

s: A Michelin-listed neighborhood restaurant named for García Márquez's hometown, blending Nordic technique with warmer flavors.
w: Arakataka takes its name from the Colombian birthplace of Gabriel García Márquez, a nod to the restaurant's willingness to let spice and acidity intrude on classic Nordic plating. Holds a Michelin listing near Youngstorget.
_facts: Named after Gabriel García Márquez's birthplace

s: A 19th-century artists' beer hall near the Royal Palace, still pulling pints under a wall of framed paintings.
w: Lorry has served as Oslo's unofficial artists' canteen since the 1870s, its walls a salon-hang of donated paintings collected over a century. It sits just off the Palace park in Majorstuen, doing straightforward Norwegian pub food alongside one of the city's largest beer lists.
_facts: Near the Royal Palace, Majorstuen area

s: A pork-obsessed dining room near St. Olavs plass, built around a multi-day slow-cooked knuckle.
w: Den Glade Gris -- 'the happy pig' -- commits fully to its name: the signature dish is a ham hock marinated and slow-cooked over several days until it falls off the bone. A straightforward, unpretentious room on St. Olavs gate.
_facts: Signature dish: slow-cooked pig knuckle (multi-day preparation)

s: Two Michelin stars on the upper floor of a renovated building in Møhlenpris, run on dry-aging and charcoal.
w: Chef Kristian Vangen and manager Øystein Ellingsen built Gaptrast around dry-aged and preserved local ingredients finished hard over charcoal, on the top floor of a fully renovated Baneveien building, with the more casual Bark below.

s: The ground-floor wine bar beneath Gaptrast, sharing its building and its kitchen's sourcing but a looser, bistro register.
w: Bark opened on the ground floor of the same Møhlenpris building as its upstairs sibling Gaptrast, run by the same team under chef Kristian Vangen. It trades tasting-menu formality for a Nordic small-plates-and-wine format.
_facts: Same building and ownership as Gaptrast

s: An omakase counter tucked inside a modern art museum, sushi and yakitori served where visitors used to get only coffee.
w: Hos Bobby opened in 2026 inside KODE's Stenersen building, turning what was previously gallery and café space into the city's newest omakase address. Chef Bobby Buaprakone runs a tight counter of nigiri, raw langoustine, and yakitori a few steps from the museum's galleries.
_facts: Opened 2026 inside KODE Stenersen art museum building

s: An 18-course tasting menu inside a silver ellipsoid moored in the middle of the Hardangerfjord, reached only by electric boat.
w: Iris operates inside Salmon Eye, the world's largest floating art installation, its dining room submerged partly below the waterline in the Hardangerfjord off Rosendal. Chef Anika Madsen's 'Expedition Dining' starts with a boat crossing to her boathouse on Snilstveitøy; it won its first Michelin star in the 2024/2025 cycle.
_facts: Housed in 'Salmon Eye', world's largest floating art installation
Accessible only by electric boat from Rosendal

s: A working farm on the shore of Raftsundet where Michelin's northernmost star hangs on cabbage, sheep, and the tide.
w: Chef Halvar Ellingsen cooks in the same Vesterålen farm buildings his great-great-great-grandfather lived in, drawing the tasting menu almost entirely from land and water he can see from the kitchen door. In June 2026 Kvitnes Gård became the first restaurant north of the Arctic Circle to hold a Michelin star.
_facts: World's northernmost Michelin-starred restaurant, awarded June 2026
Chef Halvar Ellingsen, cooking on his family's historic farmland

a: Shlomo Hamelech St, corner King George St
s: A corner falafel stand off King George Street where the pavement queue rarely breaks, at any hour of the day.
w: Ariel Rosenthal opened HaKosem in 2001 on the corner of King George and Shlomo Hamelech streets, a few doors from Dizengoff Center. The falafel is fried to order and stuffed into pita alongside a crowded bar of pickles, salads and tehina rather than pre-dressed.

s: One circular counter for nineteen diners, wrapped around chef Raz Rahav's open kitchen on a quiet residential street below Carmel Market.
w: OCD serves a single nineteen-course tasting menu to exactly nineteen guests a night, all seated at one continuous counter that circles the kitchen. Chef Raz Rahav builds the menu on Mediterranean technique layered with Jewish and Israeli culinary references. Reservations run five to six months out.
_facts: 19-course tasting menu, 19 seats at one circular counter

a: Mendele Mokher Sfarim St, Kerem HaTeimanim
s: A bright dining room finished in rough, local textures a few steps from the edge of Carmel Market.
w: Chef Yossi Shitrit opened Mashya in 2015, building the same live-fire, market-driven repertoire he later shaped at Onza and Kitchen Market. The room deliberately echoes the raw materials of the market stalls just outside.
_facts: Chef Yossi Shitrit (also Onza, Kitchen Market)

q: Alena restaurant Norman Hotel Tel Aviv
s: The ground-floor kitchen of two restored 1920s townhouses on Nachmani Street, inside the White City's UNESCO conservation area.
w: Alena runs out of the Norman Hotel's two conjoined 1920s townhouses, among the Bauhaus buildings that give Tel Aviv's White City its UNESCO listing. The kitchen keeps to a market-driven Mediterranean menu, plated in rooms that preserve the buildings' original detail.
_facts: Located in The Norman Hotel (restored 1920s townhouses)
Within the White City UNESCO conservation zone

a: Sderot Yitzhak Rabin, Cinema City complex, Malha
s: A live-fire meat theater built into the Cinema City entertainment complex, out past the Malha train station.
w: Pitmaster's Jerusalem branch operates inside the Cinema City complex, pairing whole-animal butchery with tableside carving rather than kitchen-plated cuts. Kosher; free validated parking in the Cinema City garage.

s: A Japanese-Asian kitchen fitted into a Rehavia townhouse, named for the street number that also marks its unlabeled door.
w: Azia 19 takes its name straight from its address -- 19 Aza Street, Rehavia -- and runs out of a converted residential building with no street-facing sign. A kosher menu of sushi and pan-Asian small plates, built through word of mouth and delivery rather than passing foot traffic.
_facts: Named for its street address, Aza St 19

s: The newest kitchen on Ben Sira Street, built inside Jerusalem's adults-only Nucha hotel by the team behind Angelica.
w: Zahara opened inside the Nucha Hotel on Ben Sira Street as the younger sibling to Angelica, a Jerusalem kitchen with sixteen years behind it. Chef Roee Achdut runs a kosher, Mediterranean menu built on French technique and Asian seasoning.
